A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, proof appendix, and response-example appendix are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mistral fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, PairRM comparisons, and a batch-size ablation.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds Llama-3-8B SPPO results in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the SPPO regression objective, response selection, and constant log-partition approximation are retained. The Llama-3 experiments apply the existing procedure to another backbone.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback prompts and evaluate on AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, the same six Open LLM Leaderboard datasets, and PairRM comparisons. Adding Llama-3 changes model coverage, not the represented datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 add Llama-3-8B-Instruct as a base-model comparator; v1 included it only in Table 2's leaderboard comparison. Existing comparator memberships are otherwise retained. Newly discussed REBEL and IPO-MD are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 adds a Llama-3-8B training and evaluation configuration using the existing data split and hyperparameters. The Mistral training budget, generation procedure, model selection, evaluation metrics, and test-time reranking settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The batch-size ablation in Figure 4, MT-Bench category analysis, PairRM comparison matrix, and Appendix B response examples retain their evidence. The added Llama benchmark results do not introduce a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions mention different random seeds for sampling five responses per prompt. Neither adds repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: v4 substantially extends the results with a Llama-3 baseline and three SPPO iterations. Table 1 reports LC win rates increasing from 22.92% to 38.77%, and raw win rates from 22.57% to 39.85%; Table 3 reports average scores increasing from 68.37 to 70.29. These are new backbone-specific results; the existing Mistral results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 3.3 corrects the opponent response distribution from pi to pi-prime. Appendix A revises square-root terms in the intermediate bound and changes the Taylor remainder from o(eta) to O(eta squared). Theorem 4.1 and its convergence-rate conclusion are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement extend the empirical claims to Llama-3-8B, including its 38.77% LC win rate. The central claims about Nash-equilibrium learning, separate likelihood control, and avoiding additional strong-model supervision remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds concrete limitations concerning model expressiveness, generated-data coverage, and possible inaccuracy of the constant log-partition approximation. It also acknowledges restricted dataset and benchmark validation. Existing interpretations concerning length bias and alignment tax are retained.

D1.justification: v4 newly states that SPPO code is available and supplies a repository link. It also identifies the Llama checkpoint and explicitly documents reuse of the split and hyperparameters. Previously reported hardware and Mistral implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references and discussion for REBEL, IPO-MD, and Hedge, and elaborates SPO's relationship to the shared exponential update. This refines the positioning: v1 already acknowledged the equivalent idealized SPO framework and discussed DNO.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work discussion receive localized rewrites and reordering, while the conclusion is shortened and gains limitations and acknowledgements. Model names become more explicit. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 gain Llama rows or blocks, Table 3 is relocated relative to the figures, and several labels and captions identify Mistral explicitly. Figure 3 adds highlighting around SPPO Iter3. Existing visual formats and appendix tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Llama experiments strengthen the empirical case beyond one training backbone, while the new limitations, clearer prior-work distinctions, and mathematical corrections improve transparency and precision. The gains remain incremental: the Llama experiments lack matched DPO/IPO comparisons, and Table 1 retains an unqualified highest-win-rate claim for Mistral despite the higher Llama result.
